mcqs.question: Which statement best describes the property of gases called "filling available space"?

options.A: Gases take the shape of their container but not the whole volume.
options.B: Gases expand to occupy the entire volume of their container.
options.C: Gases have a fixed volume regardless of the container.

mcqs.answer: Gases expand to occupy the entire volume of their container.
mcqs.explanation: A gas has no fixed shape or volume; its particles move freely and spread out until they occupy every part of the space available. Therefore, it always fills the whole container. Options A, C, and D describe properties of solids or liquids, not gases.

mcqs.question: Why can gases flow like liquids?

options.A: Because their particles are tightly packed.
options.B: Because the particles are far apart and can slide past each other.
options.C: Because gases are solid at room temperature.
options.D: Because gases have a fixed shape.

mcqs.answer: Because the particles are far apart and can slide past each other.
mcqs.explanation: In a gas, particles are widely spaced and move independently, allowing them to move past one another easily. This freedom gives gases the ability to flow. Option A describes liquids, C is incorrect, and D contradicts the nature of gases.

mcqs.question: Which definition correctly describes the compressibility of gases?

options.A: Gases cannot be reduced in volume under pressure.
options.B: Gases can be reduced in volume when pressure is applied.
options.C: Gases expand when pressure is applied.
options.D: Gases have a constant volume regardless of pressure.

mcqs.answer: Gases can be reduced in volume when pressure is applied.
mcqs.explanation: Compressibility means a substance’s volume decreases when external pressure increases. Gases, because their particles are far apart, can be pushed closer together, reducing volume. Options A and D deny compressibility, while C describes expansion, the opposite effect.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of a gas at room temperature?
mcqs.explanation: Oxygen, carbon dioxide, and water vapor are all gases at typical room temperature. Ice is the solid form of water, not a gas. Therefore, D is the correct choice.

mcqs.question: A balloon released into the air will:

options.A: Keep its original shape regardless of surroundings.
options.B: Take the shape of the container it is in.
options.C: Change its shape to match the surrounding air pressure.

mcqs.answer: Change its shape to match the surrounding air pressure.
mcqs.explanation: Gases have no fixed shape; they adopt the shape of whatever space they occupy. A balloon expands or contracts until the internal gas pressure balances the external air pressure, demonstrating the property of having no fixed shape. Options A and D describe solids, while B refers to liquids filling a container.

mcqs.question: If a gas is placed in a larger empty container, what will happen to its volume?

options.A: It will remain the same as before.
options.C: It will increase to fill the container.

mcqs.answer: It will increase to fill the container.
mcqs.explanation: Because a gas has no fixed volume, its particles spread out to occupy all available space. When the container becomes larger, the gas expands until it fills the new volume. Options A and B contradict the nature of gases, and D is nonsensical.

mcqs.question: A student thinks that a gas will only occupy half of an empty bottle because it "doesn't need" the rest. Which statement correctly addresses this misconception?

options.A: The gas will occupy only half because its particles are few.
options.B: The gas will fill the entire bottle because gas particles spread out to fill all available space.
options.C: The gas will rise to the top and leave empty space below.
options.D: The gas will stay at the bottom of the bottle.

mcqs.answer: The gas will fill the entire bottle because gas particles spread out to fill all available space.
mcqs.explanation: Gases always expand to occupy the whole volume of their container, regardless of how many particles are present. This corrects the misconception that a gas might leave empty space. Options A, C, and D are incorrect interpretations of gas behavior.

mcqs.question: If a gas is released from a small opening into the atmosphere, why does it spread out quickly?

options.A: Because gas particles are heavy and fall down.
options.B: Because gas particles are far apart and move freely, allowing them to flow and mix.
options.C: Because gas particles are attracted to each other.
options.D: Because gas particles are fixed in place.

mcqs.answer: Because gas particles are far apart and move freely, allowing them to flow and mix.
mcqs.explanation: The large separation between gas particles and their random, rapid motion enable them to move outward and mix with surrounding air, demonstrating the ability of gases to flow. Options A, C, and D describe properties not true for gases.
